R01.text: Over the 14-day window, sleep start shifted abruptly from ~22:50 to ~01:10 while wake time remained fixed at 07:00, reducing mean sleep duration by 138 minutes (469 to 331). Steps fell 67% (7985 to 2643). Activity duration (~55 min), low movement (~450 min), resting heart rate (~56 bpm), and RMSSD (~45 ms) stayed near baseline. Evening activity intervals persisted daily. No recovery was observed.

R02.text: During your 28-day baseline you slept ~469 min nightly (starting ~22:50, waking 07:00) with ~8,000 steps and ~54 active minutes. In the past 14 days, sleep start shifted to ~01:08 and duration fell to ~331 min, while wake time stayed at 07:00. Steps dropped to ~2,643/day, but activity minutes held steady at ~55. Resting heart rate (~56 bpm) and HRV (~45 ms) remained near baseline. The shorter sleep reflects delayed sleep onset rather than earlier waking, while maintained activity minutes alongside fewer steps suggest altered movement patterns.

unsupported_interpretations.claim_excerpt: maintained activity minutes alongside fewer steps suggest altered movement patterns
unsupported_interpretations.why_unsupported: The raw data shows steps decreased while activity duration remained stable, but inferring 'altered movement patterns' requires knowledge of activity type or intensity which is not recorded. K050 notes steps may miss non-step exercise, but this does not confirm a pattern change occurred.
unsupported_interpretations.raw_data_context: metrics.steps decreased from mean 7985 to 2643; metrics.activity_duration_minutes changed from 54.4 to 55.4. activity_intervals intensity is 'unknown' throughout.

unsupported_interpretations.claim_excerpt: reduced nighttime wearable coverage from 490 to 350 minutes coinciding with later sleep start times
unsupported_interpretations.why_unsupported: While coverage did decrease and sleep start shifted later, attributing the coverage reduction specifically to the later sleep start assumes a causal or mechanical link not established by the data alone. The quality policy defines coverage requirements but does not explain why coverage changed.
unsupported_interpretations.raw_data_context: nighttime_coverage_minutes decreased from 482-497 range to 342-358 range. metrics.sleep_start_at shifted from ~22:50 to ~01:10.

unsupported_interpretations.claim_excerpt: low movement minutes unchanged near 450 per day while steps decrease by over 5000 indicating reduced ambulation without increased sedentary time
unsupported_interpretations.why_unsupported: K068 explicitly states that low-movement estimates should not be relabelled as confirmed sitting or sedentary behaviour without posture measurement. Equating unchanged low movement minutes with 'without increased sedentary time' oversteps the available data.
unsupported_interpretations.raw_data_context: metrics.low_movement_minutes baseline mean 448.6, window mean 451.1. metrics.steps decreased by 5342. No posture data exists.
